newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Esprit in Indonesian venture, rights.
newsitem.headline: Esprit in Indonesian venture, rights.

text.p: Malaysian construction company Esprit Group Bhd said on Thursday it proposed to participate in the development of an Indonesian highway, and would also undertake a rights issue.

Esprit said it would enter into a joint venture with the Indonesian Highway Authority P.T. Jasa Marga and a local company P.T. Mawatindo to undertake the privatisation of the proposed Semarang-Demak toll road.
The company also announced a right issue of 22 million new shares on a one-for-one basis at 5.95 ringgit each, and the rights issue of 132 million irredeemable, convertible loan stock (ICULS).

Esprit said it would acquire a 75 percent stake in L.H. Letrik, a Malaysian cable and switchgear maker, costing 1.098 million ringgit, to be satisfied by the issue of 1.41 million new Esprit shares at the issue price of 7.80 ringgit each.
Esprit also announced the acquisition of a 65 percent stake in Westform TeChnologies Sdn Bhd for 8.8 million ringgit, and 60 percent of I-Mix Concrete Industries Sdn Bhd for 7.7 million ringgit.

Westform's acquisition would be satisfied by an issue of 1.12 million new Esprit shares at 7.80 ringgit each, while the purchase of I-Mix would be settled by the issue of 987,743 new Esprit shares also at 7.80 ringgit each.
Esprit also said it planned to buy the entire paid-up capital of Guobena Development Sdn Bhd for 56 million ringgit.
The toll road is to be built in central Java and is due to stretch 24 kilometres. the project is expected to cost 515 billion rupiah, with a concession period of 30 years.
Esprit shares which have been suspended since June 4, would be requoted on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange on Friday.
